🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Use "there is" and "there are" to say what exists in a place.
- Choose between singular and plural forms correctly.
- Make negatives and questions with "there is / there are".
- Use "some", "any", "a" and numbers together with these structures.

🔍 Warm-up
Look around your classroom. Can you finish these sentences?
- There is a ______ on the wall.
- There are ______ students in the room.
This lesson teaches you exactly how to describe what is in a place.

I. What "there is / there are" means
📘 Rule (functions)
We use "there is" and "there are" to say that something EXISTS or is PRESENT in a place. It is the natural way to describe a room, a town, a picture, or a situation.
- There is a park near my house.
- There are many shops in the city centre.

👀 Note
Do not confuse "there is" (existence) with "it is" (identifying something). 
- There is a book on the desk. (a book exists there)
- It is my English book. (I say which book it is)

II. Singular and plural

<rect x="255" y="40" width="150" height="34" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6"/>
<text x="330" y="62" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">there + be</text>
<line x1="330" y1="74" x2="170" y2="110" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<line x1="330" y1="74" x2="490" y2="110" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<rect x="60" y="110" width="220" height="34" rx="8" fill="#16a34a"/>
<text x="170" y="132" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">There is + singular</text>
<text x="170" y="166" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">There is a park near my house.</text>
<text x="170" y="184" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">There is an apple on the table.</text>
<rect x="380" y="110" width="220" height="34" rx="8" fill="#e11d48"/>
<text x="490" y="132" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">There are + plural</text>
<text x="490" y="166" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">There are three windows here.</text>
<text x="490" y="184" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">There are some children outside.</text>
<rect x="80" y="205" width="500" height="40" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
<text x="330" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">Look at the noun AFTER the structure to choose is/are.</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📏 Form (affirmative)
- There is + singular noun. (there's)
- There are + plural noun.

✏️ Worked examples
- There is a computer in the office.
- There is an apple on the table.
- There are three windows in this room.
- There are some children in the garden.

🛠️ Method: is or are?
Step 1 — Look at the noun AFTER the structure.
Step 2 — If it is singular (one thing), use "There is".
Step 3 — If it is plural (more than one), use "There are".
Example: ___ five books → books is plural → There are five books.

📏 Lists
When we list several things, the verb usually agrees with the FIRST item.
- There is a sofa, two chairs and a table in the living room.

⚠️ Common mistakes
- There is many people → There are many people (people is plural).
- There are a car → There is a car (a car is singular).

III. Negatives
📏 Form (negative)
- There is not (there isn't) + singular.
- There are not (there aren't) + plural.

✏️ Worked examples
- There isn't a cinema in my village.
- There aren't any hospitals near here.

📘 Rule (any in negatives)
In negative sentences we use "any", not "some".
- There aren't any eggs in the fridge.
- There isn't any water in the bottle.

IV. Questions and short answers

[[FIG]]<svg viewBox="0 0 680 260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="340" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Affirmative — Negative — Question</text>
<rect x="20" y="45" width="200" height="150" rx="8" fill="#16a34a" opacity="0.12" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="120" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Affirmative</text>
<text x="120" y="95" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">There is a book.</text>
<text x="120" y="115" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">There are two books.</text>
<text x="120" y="145" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">use "some"</text>
<rect x="240" y="45" width="200" height="150" rx="8" fill="#e11d48" opacity="0.12" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="340" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Negative</text>
<text x="340" y="95" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">There isn't a book.</text>
<text x="340" y="115" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">There aren't any books.</text>
<text x="340" y="145" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">use "any"</text>
<rect x="460" y="45" width="200" height="150" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6" opacity="0.12" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="560" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Question</text>
<text x="560" y="95" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">Is there a book?</text>
<text x="560" y="115" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">Are there any books?</text>
<text x="560" y="145" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">use "any"</text>
<text x="340" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">How many students are there in your class? — There are twenty-eight.</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📏 Form (questions)
- Is there + singular ? — Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
- Are there + plural ? — Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

✏️ Worked examples
- Is there a library in your school? — Yes, there is.
- Are there any restaurants in this street? — No, there aren't.
- How many students are there in your class? — There are twenty-eight.

📘 Rule (some / any)
- Use "some" in affirmative sentences: There are some flowers.
- Use "any" in negatives and questions: There aren't any flowers. / Are there any flowers?

🛠️ Method: building a question about a place
Step 1 — Start with Is there (singular) or Are there (plural).
Step 2 — Add "a / an" (singular) or "any" (plural).
Step 3 — Add the noun and the place.
Step 4 — Add a question mark.
Example: Are there any parks in your town?

👀 Note
To ask about quantity, use "How many ... are there?"
- How many books are there on the shelf?

✏️ Worked description

<rect x="60" y="50" width="540" height="150" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/>

<rect x="330" y="140" width="60" height="30" rx="4" fill="#3b82f6" opacity="0.3"/>
<text x="360" y="162" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">table</text>
<circle cx="500" cy="150" r="20" fill="#e11d48" opacity="0.35"/>
<text x="500" y="155" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">fountain</text>

There is a big garden behind my house. In the garden there are two trees and some beautiful flowers. There is a small table where my family drinks tea. There isn't a swimming pool, but there is a little fountain. There are birds in the trees every morning.

⚠️ More common mistakes
1. Forgetting "any" in questions/negatives: Are there some shops? → Are there any shops?
2. Using "have" instead: In my room have a bed → In my room there is a bed.
3. Wrong short answer: Are there...? — No, there isn't → No, there aren't.

⭐ Recap
- "There is" + singular; "There are" + plural.
- The verb agrees with the noun that follows it.
- Negatives: there isn't / there aren't + any.
- Questions: Is there...? / Are there...? + short answers.
- "some" for affirmative, "any" for negatives and questions.

📘 Language bank
Places: room, house, town, city, village, park, school, shop, hospital, library, garden.
Objects: table, chair, bed, window, door, computer, book, tree, flower.
Quantifiers: a, an, some, any, many, a lot of, numbers.
Useful sentences: There is a park near my house. / There are some shops in the street. / Is there a library here? / Are there any restaurants nearby? / How many students are there in your class?

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Complete with "is" or "are".
1. There ______ a big tree in the garden.
2. There ______ three windows in my room.
3. There ______ some milk in the fridge.
4. There ______ many students in the class.
5. There ______ a computer on the desk.

Exercise 2 — Make these sentences negative.
1. There is a cinema in my town.
2. There are some shops in this street.
3. There is a park near the school.
4. There are eggs in the box.

Exercise 3 — Write questions with "Is there" or "Are there".
1. ______ a library in your school?
2. ______ any restaurants near your house?
3. ______ a swimming pool in your town?
4. How many students ______ in your class?

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: 1. is 2. are 3. is 4. are 5. is.
Exercise 2: 1. There isn't a cinema in my town. 2. There aren't any shops in this street. 3. There isn't a park near the school. 4. There aren't any eggs in the box.
Exercise 3: 1. Is there 2. Are there 3. Is there 4. are there.

🗣️ Speaking task
Describe your bedroom or your classroom to a partner. Use "There is..." for single things and "There are..." for plural things. Include at least five sentences and one negative (There isn't... / There aren't any...).

👀 Extra note
The safest way to avoid mistakes: always look at the noun that comes AFTER the structure.
- One thing → There is / Is there / There isn't.
- More than one → There are / Are there / There aren't.
And remember: "some" in positive sentences, "any" in negatives and questions.

🌍 Real-life English
"There is" and "there are" are everywhere in daily life. When you describe your home, you say "There is a kitchen, a living room and two bedrooms." When you talk about your town, you say "There is a market and there are many cafés." When you look at a photo, you describe it the same way: "There are three people and there is a dog." Try this: look around the room you are in now and make five sentences, mixing singular ("There is a...") and plural ("There are some..."), and one negative ("There isn't a..."). This structure is one of the fastest ways to start describing the world around you in English.

📋 Summary
- Use "there is" and "there are" to say that something exists or is present in a place.
- "There is" + singular noun; "there are" + plural noun — always look at the noun AFTER the structure.
- Negatives: there isn't (singular) / there aren't (plural) + any — never use "some" in negatives.
- Questions: Is there...? / Are there...? — with short answers (Yes, there is. / No, there aren't.).
- Use "some" in affirmative sentences and "any" in negatives and questions.
- Ask about quantity with "How many ... are there?"
- Don't confuse "there is" (existence) with "it is" (identifying something specific).
- "There is/are" is one of the most useful structures for describing a room, a town or a picture.

Look at the things in Sami's room: one book, one lamp, one computer and one schoolbag.

Complete the sentences with There is, then answer.
1) ______ a book on the table.
2) ______ a lamp next to the computer.
3) The schoolbag is under the table. Write a sentence that begins with There is.
4) Choose the right word: we use “There is” with a (singular / plural) noun.

Read the notes about Mariem's classroom.
| Thing | Number |
|---|---|
| windows | 3 |
| door | 1 |
| desks | 15 |
| board | 1 |

Use the table to complete the sentences with There is or There are.
1) ______ three windows in the room.
2) ______ a door.
3) ______ fifteen desks.
4) Write one sentence about the board.

Look at the list of animals in Uncle Hedi's garden: one cat, two dogs, no horse, no birds.

Answer the questions with a short answer (Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. / Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.).
1) Is there a cat in the garden?
2) Is there a horse in the garden?
3) Are there two dogs in the garden?
4) Are there any birds in the garden?

Youssef is looking in his schoolbag before the English lesson.
Youssef: Oh no! There is a book in the bag and there are some pencils, but I can't find my other things!

Make these sentences negative to say what is missing.
1) There is a pen in the bag.
2) There is a ruler in the bag.
3) There are some notebooks in the bag.
4) Write the short forms of: there is not / there are not.
Choose: There (is/are) some milk in the fridge.
Complete: ___ any chairs? — No, there aren't.

Ines writes about her grandfather's garden, but she makes mistakes with there is / there are.
My grandfather has a nice garden. (a) There are a dog in the garden. (b) There is two orange trees near the door. (c) There are a small table under the trees. (d) There are many flowers.

1) Find the three wrong sentences and the correct sentence.
2) Rewrite the wrong sentences correctly.
3) Explain your correction of sentence (a) in a few words.

Hatem is visiting the new school library. He asks the librarian some questions.

Use the words to write Hatem's questions with Is there ...? or Are there ...?
1) (books / on the shelf)
2) (a computer / in the library)
3) (dictionaries / on the table)
4) The librarian says yes to question 1 and no to question 2. Write her two short answers.
When do we use "there is" and "there are"?
Describe your desk using there is/are (one sentence).
